options.text: Both taps have equal pressure, because the height of water above each tap is the same.
The tap from tank Q has greater pressure, because tank Q holds more water in total.
The tap from tank P has greater pressure, because a narrower tank always gives greater pressure.
Both taps have equal pressure only if the tanks hold equal amounts of water.

stem:
The diagram shows Leela's two overhead tanks. Tank P is tall and narrow; Tank Q is short and wide and holds more water in total. In both tanks the water surface is 3.0 m above an identical ground-floor tap.

Both taps are opened fully. Which claim about the water pressure at the taps is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Liquid pressure at a bottom tap depends on the height of liquid above the point. Equal heights give equal pressure even when one tank holds more water because it is wider.
teacher.figure_note: Two tanks, equal 3.0 m water height above taps; Q wider with more total water.
